::: {.callout-important}
## 本节考纲要求

考生需要能够：

1. 使用 $\sum r$、$\sum r^2$、$\sum r^3$ 的标准结果求相关级数；
2. 使用 method of differences 求有限级数之和，必要时先作部分分式分解；
3. 直接考察前 $n$ 项和，判断级数是否收敛，并在收敛时求无穷和。
:::

## 学习路线

::: {.study-card}

- [ ] 能从通项写出前几项，并从具体级数识别通项和求和上下限
- [ ] 能正确拆分求和符号并使用三个标准公式
- [ ] 能通过错位相减处理等比型有限和
- [ ] 能将有理式裂项，使中间项成对消去
- [ ] 能保留所有未消去的首项和尾项
- [ ] 能从 $S_n$ 在 $n\to\infty$ 时的极限判断收敛并求无穷和

:::

## 1. 教材知识点

### 1.1 Sequences, series and sigma notation

数列是按顺序排列的数；级数是数列各项的和。若通项为 $u_r$，前 $n$ 项和写作

$$
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r.
$$

上下限决定所包含的项。若求和式中没有 $r$，仍需按上下限重复相加，例如

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}c=nc.
$$

若已知前 $n$ 项和，则

$$
u_1=S_1,\qquad u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}\quad(r\ge2).
$$

### 1.2 Standard results

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1),
$$

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^2=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1),
$$

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^3=\frac14n^2(n+1)^2.
$$

使用时先展开通项，再利用求和的线性性质。不要把 $\sum r^2$ 误写成 $\left(\sum r\right)^2$。

### 1.3 Changing limits

对于连续的一段整数，可用“大和减小和”：

$$
\sum_{r=a}^{b}u_r
=\sum_{r=1}^{b}u_r-\sum_{r=1}^{a-1}u_r.
$$

同理，若 $S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r$，则

$$
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n.
$$

### 1.4 Method of differences

核心是把通项写成相邻项之差：

$$
u_r=f(r)-f(r+1).
$$

于是

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r
=[f(1)-f(2)]+[f(2)-f(3)]+\cdots+[f(n)-f(n+1)],
$$

中间项全部消去，只剩

$$
\boxed{S_n=f(1)-f(n+1)}.
$$

若裂项跨度大于 1，通常会留下多于一个首项和尾项，必须将前几项与最后几项完整写出。

### 1.5 Sum to infinity

先求有限前 $n$ 项和 $S_n$，再直接考察

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n.
$$

若极限存在且有限，则级数收敛，且该极限就是无穷和。若 $u_n\not\to0$，级数一定不收敛；但 $u_n\to0$ 本身不能保证收敛。

## 2. Textbook Examples

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.1 · Pages 43–44

For the series

$$
2+5+8+\cdots+500,
$$

**(i)** find a formula for the $r$th term $u_r$; **(ii)** find the number of terms; **(iii)** find the sum by reversing and adding; **(iv)** confirm the answer using sigma notation.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

The sequence has common difference $3$, so

$$
u_r=3r-1.
$$

Since $3r-1=500$, there are $167$ terms. Reversing and adding gives

$$
2S=167(2+500),
$$

so

$$
\boxed{S=41917}.
$$

Also

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{167}(3r-1)
=3\cdot\frac{167\cdot168}{2}-167
=41917.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-1"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.2 · Page 44

Calculate the sum of the integers from $100$ to $200$ inclusive.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

$$
\sum_{r=100}^{200}r
=\sum_{r=1}^{200}r-\sum_{r=1}^{99}r
=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}-\frac{99\cdot100}{2}.
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{15150}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-2"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.3 · Page 47

Given $u_r=r^2+2r-1$:

1. write down the first three terms;
2. find $\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r$;
3. check the result for $n=3$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

The first three terms are $2,7,14$. Also

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r-1)
&=\sum r^2+2\sum r-\sum1\\
&=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+n(n+1)-n\\
&=\boxed{\frac16n(2n^2+9n+1)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $n=3$, the formula gives $23$, and $2+7+14=23$.

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-3"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.4 · Page 48

Write

$$
(1\times3)+(2\times4)+(3\times5)+\cdots+n(n+2)
$$

using sigma notation, and hence find its sum.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r).
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+7)}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-4"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.5 · Page 50

Calculate

$$
5+10+20+40+\cdots+2560+5120.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Let the sum be $S$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
S&=5+10+20+\cdots+2560+5120,\\
2S&=10+20+40+\cdots+5120+10240.
\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting gives $S=10240-5$, hence

$$
\boxed{S=10235}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-5"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.6 · Pages 50–51

**(i)** Show that

$$
\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}=\frac1{r(r+1)}.
$$

**(ii)** Hence find

$$
\frac1{1\times2}+\frac1{2\times3}+\cdots+\frac1{30\times31}.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

The identity follows by combining the two fractions. Therefore

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{30}\frac1{r(r+1)}
=\sum_{r=1}^{30}\left(\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}\right)
=1-\frac1{31}.
$$

Hence the sum is

$$
\boxed{\frac{30}{31}}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-6"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.7 · Page 52

**(i)** Show that $(2r+1)^2-(2r-1)^2=8r$.

**(ii)** Hence find $\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r$.

**(iii)** Deduce the standard result for $\sum_{r=1}^{n}r$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Expanding proves the identity. Summing gives

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r
=(3^2-1^2)+(5^2-3^2)+\cdots+[(2n+1)^2-(2n-1)^2].
$$

Thus

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r=(2n+1)^2-1=4n^2+4n,
$$

and hence

$$
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1)}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-7"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2.8 · Pages 52–53

**(i)** Show that

$$
\frac2r-\frac3{r+1}+\frac1{r+2}
=\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
$$

**(ii)** Hence find

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
$$

**(iii)** Deduce the sum to infinity.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

After using the stated decomposition and writing the first and last terms, all middle terms cancel, leaving

$$
S_n=\frac32-\frac2{n+1}+\frac1{n+2}
=\frac{n(3n+7)}{2(n+1)(n+2)}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{S_\infty=\frac32}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-example-2-8"> Completed</label>
:::

## 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook

::: {.question-card}
### Exercise 2B, Question 11

It is given that

$$
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r=2n^2+n.
$$

Write down $S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4$. Express $u_r$ in terms of $r$, justifying your answer. Find

$$
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r.
$$

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

$$
S_1=3,\quad S_2=10,\quad S_3=21,\quad S_4=36.
$$

For $r\ge2$,

$$
u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}=4r-1,
$$

and this also gives $u_1=3$. Finally,

$$
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n
=\boxed{6n^2+n}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-textbook-exam-11"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 3, October/November 2013.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card}
### Exercise 2C, Question 11

Given that

$$
u_k=\frac1{2k-1}-\frac1{2k+1},
$$

express $\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k$ in terms of $n$ and deduce $\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

$$
\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k
=\left(\frac1{25}-\frac1{27}\right)+\cdots+
\left(\frac1{2n-1}-\frac1{2n+1}\right)
=\boxed{\frac1{25}-\frac1{2n+1}}.
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k=\frac1{25}}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-textbook-exam-2c11"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 1, October/November 2014.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card}
### Exercise 2C, Question 12

For positive integers $n$,

$$
a_n=\frac{n+5}{n^2-n+1}-\frac{n+6}{n^2+n+1},
$$

and $S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n$. Find $S_{30}$ correct to 3 decimal places and the least $N$ for which $S_N>4.9$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Successive terms telescope because the second fraction in $a_n$ is the first fraction in $a_{n+1}$. Thus

$$
S_N=6-\frac{N+6}{N^2+N+1}.
$$

Therefore

$$
S_{30}=6-\frac{36}{931}=\boxed{5.961}\quad\text{(3 d.p.)}.
$$

Checking successive values gives $S_2<4.9$ and $S_3>4.9$, so

$$
\boxed{N=3}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-textbook-exam-2c12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2015.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card}
### Exercise 2C, Question 13

Let $f(r)=r(r+1)(r+2)$.

1. Show that $f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)$.
2. Hence show that $\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)$.
3. Using the standard result for $\sum r$, deduce the standard result for $\sum r^2$.
4. Find the sum

$$
1^2+2(2^2)+3^2+2(4^2)+\cdots+2(n-1)^2+n^2,
$$

where $n$ is odd.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Summing $f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)$ gives

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2).
$$

Since $r(r+1)=r^2+r$,

$$
\sum r^2=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)-\frac12n(n+1)
=\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)}.
$$

For the final series, add one extra copy of every even square to the usual sum of squares. With $m=(n-1)/2$,

$$
\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+\frac23m(m+1)(2m+1)}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="series-textbook-exam-2c13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2012.</div>
:::

## 5. 完成本节的判断标准

1. 能从具体各项准确写出通项及求和上下限；
2. 能把多项式通项拆开并正确代入三个标准公式；
3. 能从部分分式或恒等式识别消项结构；
4. 能完整保留未消去的首项与尾项；
5. 能从 $S_n$ 的极限判断收敛并求无穷和。
